transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Elena Ruiz (Redwood); David Li, Anika Bose, Marcus Nguyen, Priya Sharma (Cloverfield)

Summary:
Quick kickoff-ish handoff from AE/CSM to implementation/SE team; focus on security reqs for staging/VPC, KMS integration, audit logs, and a short perf baseline to run in staging. Customer reiterated timeline to evaluate Dedicated vs Private; strong data residency and encryption needs.

Topics Covered:
- Staging/VPC network and access patterns
- KMS/HSM and key-rotation expectations
- Audit logs, retention and SOC2 questions
- Token/profile QPS for perf baseline and expected SLA
- Rollout phases and next steps for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we are, uh, excited to get this handoff, I know David mentioned timelines in the intro so we'll go through security and staging next steps, quick intros?
[00:08] David Li: hi all david here, vp eng at cloverfield, thanks for making time, we're hoping to get a staging environment up this month and a pilot early jan, maybe jan 10 to 20 window, um that's the rough target.
[00:18] Maya Chen: perfect thanks. Samir, elena, quick intros?
[00:21] Samir Patel: yeah I'm samir from customer success, i'll own ops for the pilot, coordinate access etc, triage items.
[00:27] Elena Ruiz: elena, solutions eng, i'll own the perf baseline and the VPC/network setup with your infra folks.
[00:34] Anika Bose: anika from it, we'll be handing over network and sso details, we do have some strict egress rules in staging.
[00:39] Marcus Nguyen: marcus, security architect; primary concerns: key management, audit trails, and ensuring no PHI leaks to third-party hosted logs - cloverfield does have regulated data.
[00:48] Priya Sharma: priya product, i'll coordinate prompt sets and product acceptance criteria.

[00:55] Maya Chen: great ok jumping into the checklist - first, staging topology. redwood supports private (vpc) deployments and dedicated pools; for staging most customers use a VPC-connected tenant with private endpoints - elena can you talk through what we need from cloverfield?
[01:10] Elena Ruiz: sure, we need three things up front - 1) network CIDR ranges and any NAT/proxy rules, 2) SSO/SAML metadata for user provisioning, 3) a service account or cross-account role for infra to pull logs if you want long-term retention. also note we have a small ip whitelisting nuance for the public hosted fallback.
[01:28] Anika Bose: ok on the cidr we have a staging vpc 10.22.0.0/16, but we also want to limit outbound to a proxy; can redwood operate behind a corporate outbound proxy?
[01:37] Elena Ruiz: we do support egress via proxy but there's often adjustments; we'll document the proxy handshake and cert pinning steps. it sometimes needs a small change in the runtime config.
[01:47] Marcus Nguyen: on KMS, we require customer-managed keys; we will not have plain text keys stored by third-party, and key rotation must be automated and auditable. do you support external HSM integration?
[01:59] Maya Chen: yes we have integrations for bring-your-own-kms and HSMs in private deployments, though in hosted mode we usually use envelope encryption with customer keys. note: sometimes the term 'BYOK' got garbled in older docs as 'buy ok' so watch out, ha.
[02:13] Elena Ruiz: to add, for the private control plane deployment we can plug in your KMS via mutual TLS and configure key-wrapping. i'll put the integration runbook in the doc.
[02:21] David Li: great, how much effort is the KMS hookup? we have a small infra team so want to budget time.
[02:26] Elena Ruiz: typically 2-3 days of engineer time for the initial integration, plus testing and rotation scripts; depends on your HSM vendor. if it's AWS KMS it's usually faster but HSMs vary.
[02:36] Marcus Nguyen: we use a third-party HSM (on-prem) so might be more hands-on. also, audit logs: retention policies - we need 2 years retention for security ops. can Redwood provide raw audit logs to our SIEM?
[02:48] Maya Chen: yes, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding; retention on Redwood side can be adjusted for enterprise plans, but many customers ingest into their own long-term store. we'll share the log schema - heads up the auto transcriber sometimes calls it "redwood console" as "red wood console" in older notes, ignore.
[03:02] Priya Sharma: product question - for pilot acceptance we need deterministic latency under load and no data leakage for PII fields. how do we validate this?
[03:11] Elena Ruiz: we'll run a baseline perf test: synthetic prompt profile that matches your token distribution, 2 QPS steady-state, and a burst test to 10 QPS. we'll capture p95/p99 latency and token costs. also we have eval tooling to run privacy/regression checks against a prompt set.
[03:25] David Li: can you run that in staging using our prompts? we want real traffic shape.
[03:29] Elena Ruiz: yes, please upload your sample prompts to the shared folder and we'll run a 6-hour soak test. that will surface any caching/batching behavior and costs.

[03:38] [timestamp jump]
[03:40] Anika Bose: SSO - we use Okta, SAML metadata will be shared. question: does Redwood support SCIM provisioning?
[03:47] Samir Patel: yes we support SCIM for user provisioning; we'll need admin creds or SSO metadata to set up auto-provision.
[03:53] Marcus Nguyen: about data residency - does the staging environment live in our cloud account or in Redwood-managed region? we need staging in eu-west-1 for GDPR-compliance reasons.
[04:03] Maya Chen: for private it'll be in your cloud account; for hosted we have region controls - we can pin to eu-west-1 for data locality but the control plane may be separate unless you're on private. we should map that out.
[04:15] David Li: ok leaning toward private control plane for pilot because of the residency + HSM. costing question: how different is Dedicated vs Private on pricing and ops overhead?
[04:25] Maya Chen: good q - Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood managed infra (predictable throughput), Private is customer-managed control plane and typically higher initial setup but gives you full network/control. i'll put a pricing comparison in the followup.
[04:37] Priya Sharma: any blockers we should be aware of?
[04:40] Elena Ruiz: two known friction points: 1) network egress/proxy cert pinning, 2) HSM vendor quirks for key wrapping. both addressable but need time.
[04:49] Marcus Nguyen: compliance artifacts - SOC2 report, ISO certs, penetration test summary - can you share those?
[04:55] Maya Chen: yes i'll share the security pack link, we usually send SOC2 type II and encryption whitepaper; note some items are NDAs gated but we'll start with the public summary.
[05:05] David Li: sounds good. on the perf benchmark - what metrics will you provide in the spreadsheet? token cost, p95, p99, throughput?
[05:12] Elena Ruiz: we'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, avg tokens per request, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens estimate for that model, and notes if batching changed the tail latencies.
[05:23] Samir Patel: i'll also put in the onboarding runbook steps: access, provisioning, stage validation, escalation matrix.

[05:30] [recap and next steps]
[05:31] Maya Chen: recap - action items: elena will run perf once prompts are in, samir will provision staging tenant, marcus will share SSO and cidr, maya will send security docs and pricing comparison. target: staging ready by 2026-12-20, KMS deep-dive 2026-12-22, pilot window jan 10-20. any objections?
[05:48] David Li: no objections, sounds reasonable. one ask - please include a short runbook for incident response and who to call if things go weird.
[05:55] Samir Patel: we'll include an on-call contact and escalation matrix in the runbook.
[05:58] Priya Sharma: can you also flag any changes required to our app to integrate with the SDK or call patterns?
[06:03] Elena Ruiz: yes i'll include sample SDK snippets and a small refactor checklist - mainly around streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and short-circuiting for retries.

[06:10] Maya Chen: awesome, i'll email the deck and the security pack after this. thanks everyone for the quick handoff. we'll follow up with the checklist and schedule the KMS meeting.
[06:20] David Li: thanks all.

Notes about transcript quality: there were minor transcription errors — product names occasionally split (e.g., "Red wood"), and some technical terms like HSM vendor names were obfuscated by the auto-transcriber.
